text:
maria: Heads up — billing/quotas spike for org org-42 around 09:12. Looks like repeated retries + tool calls are being double-counted. Anyone on quota accounting?

jonathan: I'm looking. Are we counting tool call input tokens separately from the host prompt? Example: user prompt -> agent -> tool prompt -> tool completion -> back to model.

sam: Yep. Current logic charges: prompt tokens (incoming request) + completion tokens (model output) + tool tokens (tool prompt + tool output). Retries re-charge entire set.

maria: That's going to blow bursts. We should probably charge only net incremental tokens on retries? e.g., if retry only affected completion tokens, don't re-charge the prompt?

anya: We already have per-key burst window reserve which deducts at start. But for retries we re-reserve again. Maybe reserve should be idempotent per request_id / idempotency_key.

jonathan: Proposed minimal change: reserve tokens at start based on input prompt + worst-case completion budget (configurable), mark reserved, then on actual usage commit actual usage and refund/rescale. That avoids double-charging on retries.

leo: Edge case: function/tool calls. If model emits a tool call then we send tool request tokens — which account should be billed? Should those be billed to original org? They are triggered by model tokens but tool may be external.

sam: Yes they should bill to the org that initiated the request. But our telemetry currently attributes tool-call tokens to the tool service account (svc-tool). That's why org saw extra usage mismatch vs console.

infra-bot: deploy-billing-agent: processed org-42 batch 1752999900: found 412 tool-call events attributed to svc-tool; re-attribute to original caller_id pending deploy.

maria: We need console to show a breakdown: prompt / completion / tool calls / retries (refunds). Right now dashboards only show total tokens which hides these anomalies.

anya: Agree. Also need to handle streaming: we stream partial completions; token accounting happens incrementally. If client disconnects mid-stream we need commit what's already sent and release reserved.

jonathan: Implementation detail idea: change RateLimiter API from reserve(n) -> ReserveID to reserve(n, idempotency_key) returning ReserveID. When retries with same idempotency_key reuse reservation. Use commit(ReserveID, used_tokens) and refund if used < reserved.

sam: Pseudocode: ```python
rid = rate_limiter.reserve(key=idem, n=estimated)
try:
  used = execute_model_and_tools()
  rate_limiter.commit(rid, used)
except RETRYABLE:
  # don't double-reserve on retry, let caller reuse idem key
  raise
```

maria: Telemetry: log fields: request_id, idem_key, reserved, committed, tool_tokens, retry_count. Also add a metric: 'tokens_refunded' per-org and an alert when refunded ratio > 5%.

leo: UX: expose in console per-route token waterfall: show reserved vs committed vs refunded, plus attribution to tool calls. Make a toggle to show/hide retries.

anya: Question: do we bill for canceled tool calls? If tool request sent but tool returns 500 quickly, we still consumed tokens on tool side (tool input + maybe a tiny output). Should we refund? I'd say commit actual usage (no punitive charge).

jonathan: Agree. Only reserve-and-commit semantics needed. But we must consider latency; reserving worst-case completion might reduce concurrency due to large reservations.

maria: We can make reserve conservative and plan-tiered: enterprise can reserve small and accept more rejections; self-serve default reserve = 2x expected completion which trades higher rejection for fewer late refunds.

sam: I'll draft an RFC with concrete changes to rate_limiter, billing-processor re-attribution, and console telemetry. Est. 3 PRs: rate-limiter, billing re-attribute, console panel.

maria: :thumbsup: Please add test vectors: streaming cancel, tool-call nested (agent->tool->agent), retry with idem_key, and cross-org attribution.

jonathan: I'll own rate-limiter patch. ETA EOD Thu. I'll start with unit tests for idempotent reserve behavior.

leo: I'll take billing-processor and funnel logs to NR, plus a migration to backfill historical mis-attributed tool tokens for the last 30 days.

anya: I'll do the console panel and update product notes + a short changelog blurb for self-serve customers.

maria: Thanks — once PRs are ready we'll coordinate rollout with #eng-releases. Also need an e2e run against Dedicated since we saw different behavior there (queues + proxy changed attribution).

infra-bot: incident-bot: created ticket BLNG-487 for org-42 billing discrepancy; linked to this thread for context.

sam: Filing RFC now: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/rl-rate-limit-token-accounting — adding test plan and schema changes.

maria: Great. Let's aim to have a small patch behind a feature flag first so we can validate with org-42 only.

jonathan: Sounds good. Will add flag: billing.token_reserve_v2 = true and expose as per-org config.

leo: FYI I'm coordinating with sales for outreach to org-42 — will ping once backfill complete.

maria: Thanks all. Closing loop here for now, will follow up in the RFC thread.
